steelman: Evening home-network congestion is one of the most common causes of robotic VoIP audio: residential ISPs throttle bandwidth during peak hours (roughly 7–10 PM), causing packet loss and jitter that force codecs such as Opus into artifact-heavy error-concealment modes. The router itself may accumulate a degraded NAT table or suffer a firmware memory leak after days of continuous uptime, both of which a simple restart clears. A senior network engineer would place 'check for evening packet loss and reboot router' near the top of any home-network VoIP troubleshooting checklist. The user's multi-year, never-failed track record of router-restart success provides strong inductive support for the same root cause now. In the absence of the offline-recording evidence, this distractor would comfortably clear a plausibility bar.
